sections.heading: Elden Ring Black Blade Kindred Boss Guide
sections.text: Black Blade Kindred Fight Strategy The Best Tips for Black Blade Kindred: Use the Stone of Gurranq spell, awarded by giving Gurranq his 6th Deathroot . This spell comes out decently fast, deals good amounts of damage, and can be used in succession. It also usually aims for the Kindred's head and can even break its poise while doing so. Lightning Spear and Frenzied Burst can work well as ranged offensive spells. For Intelligence players, Glintstone Cometshard or even just Great Glintstone Shard can work wonders. If you have enough set-up, casting Comet Azur can melt the Kindred although the boss can easily avoid it. Suggested weapons: 2 Great Omenkiller Cleavers with Strength/Occult affinity and infused with Cragblade Ash of War. Any weapon infused with Glintblade Phalanx will also work great because it can stance break the gargoyle in 3 hits of the skill. Bring some Boiled Crabs or Prawns , as they provide great boosts to one's physical defense, which may be needed as the boss hits extremely hard. Summon Latenna The Albinauric , as she can provide a constant source of damage with her arrows, as long as the player can keep the Kindred's attention. Other multi-summon Ashes like Mausoleum Soldiers or Greatshield Soldiers can work well. Summon Millicent . She is decently tanky and brings great offense against a fast and large foe like the Kindred. She can also serve as a distraction. Due to its high damage per hit, Opaline Bubbletear mixed in Flask of Wondrous Physick is recommended. It allows you to almost nullify one, and only one of its hits. Melee Users Magic and Ranged Users At the Bestial Sanctum, you can stand on the ledge to his right and most of his attacks will not reach you. He will aggressively attack the corner, but the difference in elevation will keep the attacks from connecting. However, he will eventually become unstuck, usually when a leaping attack carries him up the stairs or a jump back lands him on the opposite ledge. The railing in the corner also is an obstacle to many ranged attacks. Standing on top of the railing or on horseback can help with this, but puts you more at risk of him becoming unstuck or you falling off. It can be cheesed relatively easily at Bestial Sanctum, but its high HP and the range of the roar attack can make it very tedious. Its initial position makes it very easy to get in a single attack, and it will de-aggro easily and return to that position given enough time. Using ranged attacks, you can exploit this to safely attack once or twice, run to safety, and wait for it to return to the base of the steps and turn around. It cannot enter the Bestial Sanctum, but most of his attacks can still hit you through the walls. The roar attack can reach all the way to the Bestial Clergyman (who mercifully will ignore being hit by it), so trying to attack from inside the building is not an effective approach. But if you run all the way to the back of the Sanctum, behind the Clergyman, he will eventually de-aggro and return to his original position. Another reliable approach for this method is the right ledge. You can easily land a magic attack from there (dragon breath spells can pass through the railing as well), and have enough time to summon the horse and run away. Instead of running into the sanctum, where you might get hit with a roar before you can get to safety, run around the side of the building. There are a number of obstacles in that direction that slow him down and shield you from a roar. You can simply circle the building at your own pace, and from the other side, you can stay out of sight and see when he returns to the base of the stairs. It seems to take a shorter amount of time for him to reset, compared to hiding in the sanctum. The Black Flame incantation makes it possible for very low-level players to execute this strategy very early on in the game due to its percentage-based damage. Black Blade Kindred (Bestial Sanctum) Attacks & Counters Attack Description Counter Slam n' Swing The Kindred's sword gets turned horizontal at it's waist pointing away from it and it's left hand grips the sword's blade tip, as the sword rotates so it becomes across it's waist. The Kindred then slams all of it's blade into the ground but the sword 'bounces' to it's left afterwards. Then, it's left hand releases the sword as it's right hand swings it to it's right. The slam has very low range so if you are more than a couple of metres away, you will probably automatically avoid the slam. Otherwise, rolling in any direction is viable to dodge it. When you see the sword 'bounce' and the Kindred's left hand letting go of the blade, roll anywhere but left. Can be followed up with Sword Thrust if you are a few metres away. Power Swings The Kindred brings it's sword pointing vertically to it's right at head level while gripping it with 2 hands. sections.heading: Elden Ring Black Knife Assassin Boss Guide
sections.text: Black Knife Assassin Fight Strategy The Best Tips for Black Knife Assassin: Use the Lone Wolvesor Godrick Soldiers . Magic Glintblade can make this boss laughably easy, as it tends to dodge while the spell is casted, meaning that it does not dodge the projectile itself. MELEE USERS The Assassin can be easily staggered, and the Lone Wolves Ashes can distract her, deal a lot of damage, and leave openings to land some free hits. Otherwise, use a fast weapon to keep her staggered so she can't attack you back. They also have rather low health, so it's often worthwhile to trade damage and just plan to outlast her. The safest way to attack her is to wait for her Helmsplitter and use her recovery time to set up a backstab. You can also try parrying her, but it's not recommended as her attacks are fast and hard to predict and she tends to move around a lot. MAGIC AND RANGED USERS Intelligence: Keep your distance and use ranged attacks. You can use Spirit Ashes to distracted her, or just roll and run away to keep distance between you. Carian Slicer is a fast melee spell that deals high damage for its cost, and can be cast repeatedly to possibly stunlock the boss. Magic Glintblade (Prisoner) can be used over Pebble to counter her ability to dodge projectiles. Faith: Same strategy as stated above. Catch Flame can be used the same as way as Carian Slicer, as it deals rather high damage for its speed. Flame Sling could be useful, but her tendency to dodge could make the spell less useful. Black Knife Assassin Attacks & Counters Attack Description Counter Quick Slash Slashes her dagger in various directions, often twirling around as well Blocking can cause her to ricochet and break her out of her combo. Otherwise, dodge away and wait out the rest of the combo. This attacks is also parriable at the point when her dagger is raised above her shoulder. Lunging Stab Stabs her dagger straight ahead, either overhand or underhand Blocking can cause her to ricochet and break her out of her combo. Otherwise, dodge away and wait out the rest of the combo. Feint Attack Leaps forward with one fake counterclockwise slash followed by the real clockwise slash The first slash isn't real and can't hurt you (but also can't be parried). Wait until after it's done to dodge away or you'll get caught be the real slash. Alternatively, parry after the initial slash and as her body twists and her blade comes near to ground to her left. Spinning Retreat Spins clockwise followed by a clockwise slash, then jumps to her left Roll to your left to get distance from her and allow her to finish her combo Blade-Dragging Sweep Plunges her knife into the ground and pivots around it, followed by a clockwise slash Run a short distance away when you see her dagger enter the ground, then land a hit/backstab once the attack is finished. Alternatively, parry her towards the end of the animation as the blade comes to the ground on her left and the final set of sparkes fly. Helmsplitter Jumps in the air before slamming her dagger into the ground Roll as she starts her descent. Take advantage of the long recovery time to get in a few hits or line up a backstab. Lunging Grab Lifts her left hand above her shoulder then lunges forward. If it hits, she stabs the player in the back for massive damage Either roll towards her raised arm or stagger her as soon as you notice her lifting her hand. If you dodge successfully, this is a great opportunity to get in an attack Decoy Lunge Lunges low to her right and raising her dagger high above her shoulder, sweeps the dagger across to her left before performing a back-handed slash from low on the ground, sending sparkes flying. Run away, or parry her when her dagger is to her left, just before she drags it on the ground with sparks flying. Slashing Blade of Death Charges her dagger with red flame and fire a horizontal arc of flame at you. If it hits, continuously drains your health for a time. Usually used when the player is some distance away. Roll into the projectile as it approaches, or roll to either side. Alternative, use a shield with the Carian Retalian Ash of War equipped to parry the projectile for some extra damage. Jumping Blade of Death Charges her dagger with red flame, leaps into the air then unleashes a series of Death-imbued slashes at you. If it hits, it is likely to one-shot you. It will also continuously drains your health for a time. Usually used when the player is some distance away. Run away from her as far as possible, then dodge at the last moment in case you are caught on the edge of the Blades of Death. The hit box of this attack extends some distance forward as well as behind her. : Attack can be parried : Attack can be spell parried Black Knife Assassin (Standard) Combo Chart

If you don't have access to the strategies above, she can still be defeated by looking for the dust clouds and water deformations she leaves behind as she moves around. When she charges you (again look for the dust clouds/water deformations), always stand your ground and time your attacks to land just before she reaches you. She will sometimes aggro on you continuously, it is best to avoid these by dodging away as much as possible until she loses aggro and charges you again. sections.heading: Lore Items Related to Black Knife Assassin
sections.text: Black Knife Dagger once belonging to one of the assassins who murdered Godwyn the Golden on the Night of the Black Knives. A ritual performed on the oddly misshapen blade imbued it with the power of the stolen Rune of Death. Black Knife Armor Scale armor used by the Black Knife Assassins, forged to make no sound. Traces of power yet remain in its concealing veil, which muffles the sound of footsteps. The assassins that carried out the deeds of the Night of the Black Knives were all women, and rumored to be Numen who had close ties with Marika herself. Black Knife Tiche Legendary ashen remains. Use to summon the spirit of Black Knife Tiche. Tiche was one of the assassins who, on the night of the plot, ' imbued her black knife with the Rune of Death and slew Godwyn ' the Golden. She was the daughter of the Black Knife Ringleader, ' Alecto, and was killed protecting her mother during their flight ' from the royal capital.

sections.text: Black Knight Edredd Boss Video Guide Black Knight Edredd Fight Strategy The Best Tips for Black Knight Edredd: Use the ?? Ash Summons Use the ?? Spell Bring ?? Item NOTE : The Black Knight Edredd boss may spawn with "Golden Eyes" which makes the boss drop x5 Runes (about 400,000) upon defeating it. Melee Users The Black Knight Edredd is a fast boss in Shadow of Erdtree, equipped with a double-edged blade and wings that allow it to fly briefly or enhance the speed of its attacks. As a melee user, you must rely on agility, heavy attacks, and good timing to defeat this boss. At the start of the battle, Edredd starts with the Spinning Soaring Blade Slash. This move involves the knight spotting you from afar and flying towards you while spinning its blades. To avoid taking damage, quickly roll towards Edredd. Successfully evading it provides a brief window to counter with heavy attacks. Due to Edredd being easy to stagger, capitalize on this advantage to land multiple attacks. Once you’ve dodged the Spinning Soaring Blade Slash, stay close and maintain pressure on Edredd by doing multiple attacks. The key is to match his speed by constantly moving and dodging his blade swings. Edredd's attacks are fast but predictable, learn its patterns and be ready to evade and counter quickly. After each of its attacks, you'll often have a split second to retaliate with your heavy attacks, which can stagger the knight and interrupt its rhythm. Throughout the fight, maintain a balance between offense and defense. This tactic will gradually wear down his health. Remember to manage your stamina, as constant dodging and attacking can quickly deplete your stamina. Magic and Ranged Users Strategy Writeup for Magic Users Black Knight Edredd Attacks & Counters Attack Description Counter Aspects of the Crucible: Wings Edredd manifests golden wings and flies towards his target, spinning the twinblade. May follow up with other attacks if close-by. Roll through as he begins to dive down and punish. Slash One of his most common attacks when you're battling him in close range. This can easily be countered by dodging to the right or parrying it. Jump Attack Edredd will leap high into the air, then slam down his twinblade. Dodge roll forward; if successful, it will give you a free opportunity to heal or attack. 6-Hit Combo Black Knight Edredd will do a combo wherein he will repeatedly swing his twinblade while trying to track you. Dodge roll into the boss, and the rest of the combo will most likely miss you. Do not dodge away from the boss or on the side. Black Knight Edredd Notes & Other Trivia Pierce negation is 0 against 40 for Slash — the widest spread on any Black Knight, so thrusting weapons roughly double your effective damage over slashing ones. Standard, Strike, Magic and Fire all sit at 20, making Pierce the only genuinely strong choice. 19,584 HP and 123 defense, but Stance is a low 65 and he is parryable . He ambushes you the moment you step through the first door south of the Fort of Reprimand Site of Grace , so enter with stamina to spare. Shadow of the Erdtree Bosses Ranked

sections.text: Black Knight Commander Andreas Ashen remains in which spirits yet dwell. Use to summon the spirit of Andreas, Knight-Commander of the Black Knights. The Black Knights were the primary force of Messmer's army. Their first leader was Andreas, a man endowed with great strength and command over the powers of the Crucible, and whose spirit in these ashes dwells. Though he remained a devout follower of Messmer after his flight from the Erdtree, he would rebel after learning of his liege's serpentine nature. His righteous stand was rewarded with imprisonment in an underground tomb. Black Knight Captain Huw Ashen remains in which spirits yet dwell. Use to summon the spirit of Huw, Knight-Captain of the Black Knights. The Black Knights were the primary force of Messmer's army. Second to their first Knight-Commander was Huw, a man with agile command of both twinblade techniques and the powers of the Crucible, and whose spirit in these ashes dwells. Though a champion of the divine beast hunt, he followed his father, Andreas, into rebellion against Messmer, and like his father, he too was imprisoned in an underground tomb. Messmer mourned the loss of a brother-in-arms. Ash of War: Aspects of the Crucible: Wings This Ash of War grants an armament the Sacred affinity and the following skill: "Aspects of the Crucible (Wings): This skill originates from the lifeforms of the Crucible. Grow a golden pair of wings and take to the air before diving down at the foe, weapon first. A spinning attack is performed when wielding a twinblade." Usable on swords as well as polearms capable of thrusting (colossal weapons excepted). Black Knight Armor Armor worn by the Black Knights, servants of Messmer the Impaler. Though the engraving above the heart is a Scadutree design, it is etched in gold. A small consolation to those forced to wage a war without grace or honor. Black Knight Helm Helm worn by the Black Knights, servants of Messmer the Impaler. Black iron ornamented with gold. A rotten odor stubbornly clings to it. Perhaps it arises from the tainted nature of the blood that splattered upon it. Or perhaps it is the wearer's own blackened soul, festering after endless slaughter. sections.heading: Elden Ring Black Knight Garrew Boss Guide
sections.text: Black Knight Garrew Boss Video Guide [video coming soon] Shadow of the Erdtree Bosses Ranked Black Knight Garrew Fight Strategy The Best Tips for Black Knight Garrew: Recommended Summons: Redmane Knight Ogha Recommended Ash of War: Flame of the Redmanes Recommended Spells: Rotten Breath , Ekzykes's Decay , Lightning Spear , Black Flame , Bloodboon Other items: Opaline Bubbletear Melee Users The Black Knight Garrew is a relatively easy boss to defeat if you're playing as a melee character. Its movements are extremely slow, making its attacks easy to predict and evade. The best strategy against this boss is to utilize your agility and land heavy attacks. When the Black Knight Garrew finishes an attack, and you successfully evade it, you will have a significant window to counter with your own attacks before it launches another offensive. Keep repeating this pattern by dodging, counterattacking, and retreating until its health drops significantly. Be particularly cautious of its strongest attack: a charged mace swing. This move can deal a substantial amount of damage if not evaded properly. Watch for the knight's mace glowing yellow, which signals the incoming charged attack, and be ready to roll back to avoid it. Most of Garrew's attacks involve swinging its mace and shield at you. By maintaining your agility, dodging its slow attacks, and timing your heavy counterattacks, you can steadily wear down the Black Knight Garrew and secure victory. Magic and Ranged Users Cast Rotten Breath when you first see Garrew. It may take two volleys for him to become afflicted. Sorcerers can use items such as Marika's Soreseal , Silver Tear Mask , Two Fingers Heirloom , and Outer God Heirloom to acquire the necessary stats for rot breath. Kite him and bring him in range of an aggressive and beefy spirit ash summon like Redmane Knight Ogha . When the boss catches aggro on your summon, cast your best damaging spells and abilities. Watch out for the frog tongue animation, as it comes it quickly and hits twice. Black Knight Garrew Attacks & Counters Attack Description Counter Mace Swing Black Knight Garrew swings its mace toward you slowly. Dealing heavy damage upon impact. You can easily dodge this by rolling back once he starts waving his mace. You can also block it with your great shield. Double Mace Pound Black Knight Garrew slams its mace twice downward which creates a small damage area. Can easily be dodged by rolling back before the two slams hit the ground. Shield Bash When close, Black Knight Garrew slams his shield onto you making it a weapon. This can easily be dodged by rolling to the right just before he swings his shield. Charged Mace Slam Black Knight Garrew charges its mace with power and slams it onto you. This can be evaded by rolling to either right or left once he leaps in the air. Tongue Attack Black Knight Garrew brings his head back while glowing, then releases a long-range tongue attack which goes in the direction he is facing. This can be evaded by dodge rolling to either the right or left when you see Black Knight Garrew charging it up. Black Knight Garrew Lore, Notes & Other Trivia The tongue attack used by Garrew is also used by Black Knight Commander Andreas Spirit Ash, and it is exclusive to both of them. Voice Actor: ?? sections.heading: Elden Ring Knight of the Solitary Gaol Guide
sections.text: Blackgaol Knight Mausoleum Boss Guide Shadow of the Erdtree Bosses Ranked Knight of the Solitary Gaol Fight Strategy The Best Tips for Knight of the Solitary Gaol: You cannot use Spirit Ashes Spells that stagger can be beneficial You should get Scadutree Blessing level 1 or 2 for an easier kill: See Scadutree Fragment for the locations and where to find them Melee Users This boss can switch between a Greatsword and a Crossbow giving him an edge in melee and ranged situations. The fight against the Blackgaol Knight usually begins with a Crossbow attack. He fires up to 10 Arrows rapidly following the player's movement and he requires a brief moment to either reload or switch to the Greatsword. There are some situations where his Arrow will have a fire element to it, which can end up damaging you even if you put your shield up. While he's firing the attack, you can run to one side diagonally, or horizontally and engage him in melee combat. The crossbow gives him an advantage against melee users so it's ideal to stay within attacking distance by going up to him. You'll likely end up getting your HP drained without a fight if you stay far back while you have a melee weapon. You can also equip a shield to block his ranged attacks. At first, his attacks are slow and simple. He swings his greatsword with a powerful slash and you can stay out of his path by rolling to your right side. He holds up the sword with his right arm, and this direction gives you the biggest space to cut off his reach. If you have a shield equipped, you can use it to block his incoming attacks or attempt a parry. Both of these methods will give an opening to attack him for maybe 1 or 2 attacks, depending on how fast your attack speed is. Opt for heavy attacks or Ash of War: Giant Hunt , or any Ash of War you prefer. This will cut him off in between combos. This can eventually apply Stagger if you repeatedly hit him with heavy attacks. This boss also has an attack that is similar to the Vacuum Slice that he can combine with another half-spin thrust. You can dodge this move by rolling to your right as he approaches you, then roll forward (towards him) to get behind him. From here, you have an opening to attack him with a heavy attack. You will also notice that this boss tends to do jump attacks . If you can hit him while he's mid-air, you can knock him down and get free hits out of this opportunity. As the fight goes on, this boss will also restore its health using a Flask. You can interrupt him by using a spell like Adula's Moonblade to cancel the animation. If you find yourself needing to restore HP, make sure to do it at a safe distance and that you have enough time. He may switch to the Crossbow or do a Wide Slash attack that lets him close the gap to perform a melee attack. Another strategy here is to alternate using your shield and go on offense by attacking him as you move to your right. This will give you a moment to attack him from behind for increased damage and also makes you move away from his right weapon swings. Magic and Ranged Users Keep distance from his sword swings and use spells that can get around his input reading by using well-timed casts or the Night Comet spell. Avoiding his crossbow attack can lead to a large opening. Knight of the Solitary Gaol Attacks & Counters Attack Description Counter Arrow Barrage When there's a great distance between the player and the Blackgaol Knight, he switches to using his Crossbow and fires up to 10 arrows rapidly toward the player's location. The fight usually begins with this attack move and a sound cue can be heard as he reloads the crossbow. As soon as you hear the audio cue for the crossbow reload, run to either side of the map to outrun the stream of arrows being fired at you. Alternatively, you can also put up your shield to reduce incoming damage if your movespeed is not fast enough. Overhead Slash (like Vacuum Slice ) Using the Greatsword, he swings an attack from his back and slashes overhead to deal massive damage. Then, he follows up this move with a half-spin attack. Dodge by rolling to your right side, then roll forward as he continues with the follow-up move. If you manage to get behind him, attack him; Use a shield Jump Slash He leaps into the air and slashes down onto the ground. He stays low and crouches for a few frames after this move to recover. Dodge by rolling to either side; Use a shield. Greatsword Stab When the player loses their footing and gets staggered, he will make a quick stabbing motion with the greatsword that can finish off a player when their health is about 40% or lower. Pay attention to your stance and try not to get hit continuously. Break off his attack pattern by rolling away from him, or put your shield up if available. Quick Slash He swings the greatsword to the side, up to three times. This move is usually a 3-step attack pattern that swings once per direction and ends with an Overhead Slash. sections.text: Armor of Solitude Steel chest armor of the Knights of the Solitary Gaol. Part of a heavy armor set that covers the whole body in overlapping plates of steel, and bedecked with a black cloak. The nameless mausoleums of the realm of shadow are said to hold the spirits of warriors who lost their names, or their hearts. Greatsword of Solitude Steel greatsword wielded by the Knights of the Solitary Gaol. Through a secret rite, they relinquished their hearts for heightened battle prowess. Next, they engraved their blades with two crests: one depicting the light of birth, and the other, solitude. sections.heading: Bloodhound Knight Darriwil Boss Guide for Elden Ring
sections.text: Video Guide for Bloodhound Knight Darriwil Boss Bloodhound Knight Darriwil Fight Strategy The Best Tips for Bloodhound Knight Darriwil: Staunching Boluses can help prevent Hemorrhage The Glintblade Phalanx spell and Ash of War can decimate this boss. Use Guard Counters , but be careful as he often uses follow-up attacks and Hemorrhage can build up quickly. Melee Strategy This boss can be encountered very earily and can prove to be a rather difficult fight if unprepared. Darriwil is very aggressive and his dash move allows him to move quickly and unpredictably around the arena. Be prepared to dodge at any time, and only attack once or twice when you have the opportunity or you'll end up trading hits. Keep Your Guard Up: While you're still learning his moves, guard when you're not attacking so he doesn't dash in and surprise you with an unexpected attack. A Greatshield is particularly effective here, since most of his attacks will bounce off it and give you a chance to guard counter . Be aware though that he'll still build up Hemorrhage even if you perfectly block his attacks. Try to bait his attacks when your Hemorrhage buildup is low, block one or two attacks before attacking, then back away and try to dodge until your status bar clears. Watch For Sparks: Pay particular attention to Darriwil's Grinding Attack and Clawing Attack, where he scrapes his blade or claw along the ground to create sparks. Both of these take him some time to recover from, so after you've dodged or blocked the initial attack you'll have a chance to land a hit or two. Let It Bleed: When your Hemorrhage meter fills up, you'll take 100 damage plus 10% of your total health. But since this fight comes early in the game, that's not actually much more than a normal attack would deal. It may be worth simply taking the damage, especially if you're blocking the rest of his attacks, and focusing on killing Darriwil rather than saving yourself. Magic and Ranged Strategy Darriwil is particularly difficult for ranged players, since he tends to move so quickly and dodge so readily that it's hard to land most ranged spells or arrows. Form a Phalanx: Take advantage of Darriwil's aggression using Glintstone Phalanx which will slam into him approaches to attack. Summon the blades when you've got some distance, then when he gets close focus on not getting hit and let the magic do its work. Ash of War: Glintblade Phalanx may be an even better choice since it costs less FP and deals more Stance damage. Fake Melee: Close-range spells like Carian Slicer or Catch Flame avoid the dodging issue entirely by only attacking him when he's close by. This will require carefully sequencing your dodges and attacks, though, to make sure you aren't just trading hits. Jump and Shoot: If you're using a bow, avoid using slow skills like Mighty Shot since he's likely to dodge them. Instead, jump backwards when he approaches and fire an arrow while you're in the air to avoid his attacks and get in some damage. Attacks & Counters Attack Description Counter Bloodhound's Step Tenses up, then dashes a short distance forward. This doesn't deal damage but can position him for a surprise attack. Start guarding when you see him disappear, or prepare to dodge a follow-up attack. Swipe Jogs forward and swipes with his claw. Roll when he holds his claw out to the side. Galloping Slice Runs towards you on all fours, jumping forward and slicing in a circle. Roll to your right once you see the tip of his sword to the right of his head. This will position you near him when he's recovering and give you time to get an attack in. Arc Slash Slices his sword in a wide counterclockwise arc. Roll backwards or block. Diagonal Slash Holds his sword behind him, then swings it clockwise diagonally up. Roll when sword's tip is fully behind his body. Twirling Slam Does one quick clockwise slice, then slams his sword down in front of him. Roll backwards or block. You can get in a quick hit during the recovery period. Rising Slash Slashes his sword up, emitting sparks. Dodge once out and once in to dodge the common Falling Slash follow-up. Falling Slash Slashes his sword over his shoulder and down in front of him. Dodge in and land a hit while he recovers. Overhead Slam Holds his sword behind him briefly, then slams it down in front. Roll left or right, then get in a hit while he recovers. Jumping Slam Jumps into the air, then slams his sword down to the ground. Roll once he's at the top of his jump, then get in an attack or two. Spiral Retreat Spins twice counterclockwise while hopping away from you. Roll forward to put pressure on him while he recovers. Only the initial sword swing can hurt you. Bloodhound's Finesse Swings his sword and backflips away. Roll towards him to evade the attack or block with a shield. sections.heading: Elden Ring Bols, Carian Knight Boss Guide
sections.text: Bols, Carian Knight Fight Strategy The Best Tips for Bols, Carian Knight: Use his size to your advantage by dodging between his legs. Always keep your eye on him as he can quickly turn around to perform a follow-up Stick close to him to more easily get behind him Melee Users Success in the Bols encounter hinges on your ability to get behind him. This is helped greatly by his immense height, leaving a very large room to dodge between his legs. Most of Bols' attacks hit directly in front of him and his smashing attacks release shockwaves that fan out in front of him or the point of impact. His swings are very easy to read due to their slow speed. His combo where he drags his sword on the ground is especially punishable due to the very long wind-up. When Bols summons Greatblade Phalanx projectiles, run towards him immediately to make them fly over you as they begin flight from above his head. Magic and Ranged Users The strategy for ranged players remains largely the same, except you should fight off any tendencies to want to create distance between yourself and the enemy. Do not do this for Bols. Stay close, get behind him when you can and take your shots while he's lumbering around with his sluggish attacks. Bols, Carian Knight Attacks & Counters Attack Description Counter Stomp Raises its leg and stomps its down. He'll continue stomping the same leg until you're out of range Roll towards the leg that didn't stomp and land a hit on it Swing Swings his hammer either along the ground or down in front of him Roll towards a horizontal sweep or away from a vertical one, or else stay safe near his legs and land a hit Arm Sweep Sweeps his arm along the ground Roll towards the arm Arm Slam Slams one or both arms to the ground, creating a shockwave Get behind him or jump over the shockwave Downward Stab Plunges his blade into the ground in front of him, producing a large shockwave Get behind him when you see him raising his sword and you'll be safe from the shockwave Sword Wrench After a Downward Stab, he may wrench his sword up and out of the ground to his right Stay on his left after dodging the Downward Stab Kneeling Swing Kneels on the ground and braces itself with its hand and swings its hammer in a wide counterclockwise arc with extra reach Roll towards the hammer Mega Slam Grabs his sword with both hands and holds it above his head higher and longer than for a normal vertical swing, then slams it into the ground releasing a huge shockwave This move has a very large shockwave radius and the only safe spot is directly behind him. You can also jump over the shockwave Jumping Slam Jumps high into the air and lands with a large shockwave Roll when you see him start to descend Dragging Slash Pulls his sword to the side and then dashes forward, dragging the blade along the ground before slashing once, continuing to circle around, ending the attack with a sword slam. The wind-up animation is very long and should allow you to get behind him or give you enough time to set up a dodge between his legs as he comes at you. Be very careful after the uppercut as he may continue comboing. Another tip is to lure him to the edge of the arena. If he charges into the barrier, it will stop his charge and stun him. Greatblade Phalanx Waves his sword around, summoning three magical blades above his head which fly towards you target after a short delay. These blades have good tracking and decent travel speed These blades begin flight from high up, so it's easy to avoid them by running towards him. This will also save you from getting hit by the projectiles if he decides to roar right after summoning them Spell-parrying this attack isn't recommended, since you can only parry one blade at a time and the others will likely hit you Roar Roars, creating a large shockwave and increasing his damage by 20% for 15 seconds Get behind him if you're close or as far as possible if you're not : Attack can be spell parried Bols, Carian Knight Notes & Other Trivia Slash negation is -10 while Magic is resisted at 20, so a physical slashing build outperforms sorcery here despite the Carian name. 5,109 HP against 110 defense with only 65 Stance — he breaks quickly, though he cannot be parried . He is sealed in the Cuckoo's Evergaol , just off the road north of the Revenger's Shack Site of Grace . Bols, Carian Knight Combo Chart

sections.heading: Elden Ring Cemetery Shade Boss Guide
sections.text: Cemetery Shade Fight Strategy The Best Tips for Cemetery Shade: Use Opaline Bubbletear before entering the boss arena to ensure you'll have time to to use your Spirit Calling Bell . Use the Swift Glintstone Shard Spell to hit it, as it can easily dodge slower sorceries. Bring Stanching Boluses to prevent Hemorrhage . Melee Users Blitz it Down: Cemetery Shade has extremely low health. If you've got enough damage output and the vitality to survive a few hits, you'll probably win a fight where you just trade blows until one of you dies. Defensive Maneuvers: If you want to play defensively, equip a shield with 100% physical negation. Block its attacks and guard counter afterwards to get in damage and wear down its Stance . You can also parry its attacks, but the timing is difficult since they come in rapid succession. It can still inflict Hemorrhage through a shield, so be ready to consume a Stanching Bolus . Magic and Ranged Users Quick Attacks: Cemetery Shade tends to teleport quickly around the arena, making it hard to hit if your cast time is slow or if you're using a ranged weapon skill like the Mighty Shot . Spells that like Swift Glintstone Shard that can be cast quickly are helpful, as long as you avoid its projectile attacks. Greatbows Barrage: A hit from a Greatbow will knock Cemetery Shade down if it hits. You can ensure that it does by firing right after it teleports. It'll take enough time getting back up for you to nock another arrow and repeat the process. Cemetery Shade Attacks & Counters Attack Description Counter Teleport Vanishes and reappears elsewhere in the arena. Used either to escape when being attacked or to close distance and reposition before attacking When the shade teleports close to you, there's a brief period before it starts to attack when you can roll away or start guarding Spit Trap Blows a bubble above its head, then shoots it at you. If it hits, you're unable to move or attack for 5 seconds Roll once the bubble is a little bigger than the Shade's head Spider Grab Its head begins to glow and its spider legs wriggle as it brings it down to grab your head. Only used after Spit Trap Avoid getting hit by Spit Trap Dual Stab Draws back both blades with tips pointed downwards and stabs you with them This attack's windup is difficult to distinguish from Furious Slashing, so the safest course of action is to get far away in case it does that. If you're up for a little risk, it's usually safe to block or dodge this—it will usually teleport afterwards, but often close enough that you can still hit it with an attack Dual Slash Slashes both of its blades in a wide arc from its left to its right. Block or dodge to your right, then attack One-Two Slash Slashes once clockwise then again counterclockwise Block both attacks and then guard counter , or roll backwards Overhead Slam Slams both blades into the ground in front of it Dodge or block, then attack back. It's at its most vulnerable after this attack Pincer Attack Spreads its blades wide, then closes them in on both sides at once Because the attack comes from the sides this is a dangerous move to block. Rolling forward is more reliable Spinning Swings Slashes once from its right to its left, pauses for a moment, then slashes in the opposite direction four times in quick succession while moving forward. The long pause after the first strike gives you a chance to run away or try to stagger it out of the attack. Note that a single dodge won't get you fully out of range of its follow-up swings. Furious Slashing Draws back both blades with tips pointed upwards, slashes twice, pauses briefly, slashes five more times, then finishes with an Overhead Slam Once you see it pull back its blade, roll or run away and prepare to punish the Overhead Slam. Blocking this isn't advisable, since it will still inflict a substantial amount of Hemorrhage : Attack can be parried Cemetery Shade Notes & Other Trivia Holy negation is -20, so holy damage lands 20% harder. Pierce is the one to avoid at 35. It is immune to every status effect — poison, rot, bleed, frost, sleep and madness all fail. Three are fought and each drops a different Spirit Ash: Lhutel the Headless in Tombsward Catacombs , Twinsage Sorcerer Ashes in Black Knife Catacombs , and Kindred of Rot Ashes in Caelid Catacombs . The Tombsward version has only 781 HP and hands over Lhutel the Headless, one of the strongest summons available that early in the game. The Black Knife Catacombs fight adds several Skeletons , but only the Shade has to die to end it. All three are parryable with 70 Stance , and the rune payouts scale 2,200 / 3,500 / 6,800. sections.heading: Elden Ring Chief Bloodfiend Boss Guide
sections.text: Chief Bloodfiend Boss Video Guide Chief Bloodfiend Fight Strategy The Best Tips for Chief Bloodfiend: Recommended Spirit Ashes: Black Knife Tiche Recommended Armaments: Black Knife Recommended Ashes of War: Bloodhound's Step Recommended Spells: Rotten Breath Other items: Cerulean Hidden Tear , Opaline Bubbletear , Opaline Hardtear , Windy Crystal Tear , Stanching Boluses (to alleviate Blood Loss effect) Melee Users The Chief Bloodfiend is a boss that can be found at the end of Rivermouth Cave exploration. It can be a tough boss to defeat due to its large size combined with delayed strikes. However, this boss has a proper hitbox and predictable attack patterns which makes the fight more manageable. The Chief Bloodfiend uses a massive club and possesses a large physique, relying on brute strength rather than speed. The optimal strategy for defeating this boss is to counter every attack and retaliate in between combos. Each of its attacks results in a long recovery period, providing opportunities to counterattack after every move the boss makes. The worry during this fight is its jumping attacks, which cover a wide damage area and can be difficult to avoid if you miss your timing. The Chief Bloodfiend can also inflict Hemorrhage through skills and attacks, but luckily, this boss is weak against Poison , Scarlet Rot , and Frostbite . At the start of the battle, the Chief Bloodfiend opens the fight with a Plunge Attack where he lands towards you. Then, this is followed closely by 3 Quick Swing Attacks and finishes it off with a delayed swing. Be prepared to roll to the left to evade this opening attack, then do another roll to the left. While you're on this side, you are free to run back toward it and then roll forward for the last delayed swing. Once you've dodged, move in quickly to land a few hits before retreating to a safe distance. Another move that this boss will make is the Triple Ground Stomp where the boss will stomp the ground for 2 quick steps, and end it with one delayed stomp. To dodge this move, roll to the left in quick succession, and then watch out for the third (delayed) stomp. You can roll forward right before the foot hits the ground so you can get some free hits on the boss. This pattern of dodging and countering is key to reading the Bloodfiend's attacks. Given the boss's slow recovery times, you can take advantage of these moments to do damage. As the fight goes on, this boss will also pull off moves like Ground Slam attack where the boss jumps up high in the air and crashes on top of you. This can also be combined with a delayed Club Smash . When he's making this move, you will see him raise both hands in the air while clutching the club, and it opens its mouth right before he swings it. The moves are pretty standard and the timing for dodges is as expected. Overall, the boss gives a simple sequence, and timing your moves correctly will allow you to chip away at the Bloodfiend's health. Always be alert for its stomping attacks and be ready to dodge. By maintaining this rhythm of evasion and counterattack, you'll find that the Chief Bloodfiend, despite its power, is a manageable boss. Magic and Ranged Users This boss is susceptible to Rotten Breath. Summon black knife Tiche, and cast Rotten Breath when aggro is on your summon. Chief Bloodfiend Attacks & Counters Attack Description Counter Leaping Club Swing From a distance, once the Chief Bloodfiend spots you, it will leap through the air and swing its club towards you. Can be countered by rolling back once the Chief Bloodfiend is in the air. Double Club Swing At close range, the Bloodfiend swings at you twice with its club. Roll back twice to evade this attack. Club Smash At Close to mid-range, the Chief Bloodfiend will raise its club and smash it to the ground, creating a small damage area. Once the Bloodfiend raises its club, immediately roll to either left or right multiple times. Ground Stomp Once spotted, the Bloodfiend will jump and stomp on you. Rolling back after the Bloodfiend jumps is the best way to avoid this attack. Triple Ground Stomp Once spotted, the blood fiend will chase you while stomping on the ground three times. Back up and roll until the Bloodfiend finishes his third stomp. Chief Bloodfiend Notes & Other Trivia Slash negation is -20 while Fire sits at 40 — slashing weapons are the answer and fire is the single worst choice. 21,948 HP behind 122 defense, but only 80 Stance and fully parryable . Magic is also resisted at 20, so sorcery builds should lean on physical armaments for this one. It waits inside Rivermouth Cave , reached by heading south from the Temple Town Ruins or southwest from the Northern Nameless Mausoleum . Shadow of the Erdtree Bosses Ranked

sections.heading: Lore Items Related to Chief Bloodfiend
sections.text: Bloodfiend's Arm Weapon used by the bloodfiends. An arm pulled from the corpse of one of their kin, and wielded as a makeshift weapon. Having been sanctified by a blood ritual, this armament is capable of spraying blood stored within when executing a strong attack. Bloodfiend's Fork Weapon used by the bloodfiends. Three tines of carved bone spear the victim to provoke blood loss. A ritual implement for blood offerings to the Formless Mother. At times, the bloodfiends will spill even their own blood using these forks. Bloodfiend Hexer's Ashes Ashen remains in which spirits yet dwell. ' Use to summon the spirit of a bloodfiend hexer. ' Summoning consumes HP rather than FP. This spirit conducts bloodboon rituals with a sacred spear, casts bloodflame hexes, and takes a singular pleasure in letting the blood of foes. Long ago, a subjugated tribe discovered a twisted deity amongst the ravages of war, and they were transformed into bloodfiends. The mother of truth was their savior. Bloodfiend's Sacred Spear Greatspear of the bloodfiend hexers. One of the most significant implements used in their blood rituals. Sacred spears of blood are the instruments of communion with an outer god. The mother of truth desires a wound. Mohgwyn's Sacred Spear Trident of Mohg, Lord of Blood. A sacred spear that will come to symbolize his dynasty. As well as serving as a weapon, it is an instrument of communion with an outer god who bestows power upon accursed blood. The mother of truth desires a wound. Outer God Heirloom A talisman engraved with the lore of an outer god. Raises arcane. The clan, who lost everything in the great fires, peered upon the corpse of their ancestor, normally an act of sanctity, and saw in its shadow a twisted deity. The clan had suffered such torment that the horrible thing was taken as an object of worship. Sacred Bloody Flesh Raw meat soaked with blood. ' A delicacy of the bloodfiends. Temporarily boosts physical attack power and arcane. ' When blood loss occurs nearby, further boosts attack power. The blood is said to have fallen from the Formless Mother's wound. Never will it dry, never will it rot. Sanguine Amaryllis A bloodflower with meaty petals. Material used for crafting items. Grown by bloodfiends in pools of blood. Perhaps even the fiends admire blood's beauty. sections.heading: Elden Ring Cleanrot Knight Boss Guide
sections.text: Cleanrot Knight Fight Strategy The Best Tips for Cleanrot Knight: Don't just keep attacking over and over—once it uses Spear Guard, back off or it'll counter-attack. Use Fire Pots . It's very weak to fire and has low health to begin with, so a single pot will do a lot of damage even at low levels Long windups and attack animations leave it very vulnerable to backstabs Melee Users Baiting: Stay close and towards its left to tempt it into using Spear Stab, Impale, or Sacred Phalanx. When it starts winding up one of these slow attacks, circle around behind it and get a backstab critical. Magic and Ranged Users Waiting Game: Don't underestimate the Cleanrot Knight's range. It may not have any ranged attacks, but Rushdown is very good at closing distance and Impale will do a lot of damage if it connects. If your spells take a while to cast, either make sure you're across the arena or it's distracted by your summons. Cleanrot Knight Attacks & Counters Attack Description Counter Slash Swings the sword in its right hand Block, roll backwards, or roll in the direction of the swing Jab Pulls back its right arm, then quickly stabs forward with its sword Roll to either side when you see its right arm pull back Triple Jab Pulls back its right arm, then stabs forward twice quickly, then once more after a brief pause Roll to either side when you see its right arm pull back Spear Variant Spear Stab Pulls its spear back for a second, then stabs it forward Roll to either side as you see its spear pass its head. If you have a quick weapon, you can get in a hit while it winds up Twin Stab Holds both its swords and spear pointing forward for a second, then stabs them both together in front of it This doesn't have a lot of forward range, so you can easily move away during its long windup Rushdown Levels the spear to the ground while it glows golden, then sprints forward with it extended. Followes up with Impale. Roll to either side as soon as you see the spear start glowing Impale Thrusts the spear forward and up. If this hits, it will impale you and instantly inflict Scarlet Rot Roll to either side when you see it pull back its spear, and avoid getting hit by Rushdown Spear Guard Crosses its spear and sword in front of its chest, blocking attacks from the front Keep your distance and wait for it to put its guard down before attacking again Golden Shove If hit while guarding or when an enemy is too close, it retaliates by shoving its weapons forward. Back away when you see it cross its weapons and wait for it to drop its guard. Alternatively, use this opportunity to heal or fire off some spells. Sacred Phalanx Lets its spear fall down behind it to its left, then drags it forward, leaving a golden glow on the ground that erupts into holy spears in a straight line. Roll around it clockwise, as its right flank is unprotected during this attack. Make sure to avoid the golden glow on the ground Retreating Phalanx Extends its spear forward and to its right, then drags it counterclockwise behind it while it steps backwards, leaving a golden glow on the ground that erupts into holy spears Keep back and avoid the golden glow on the ground, then close back in once the holy spears have vanished : Attack can be parried Cleanrot Knight Notes & Other Trivia They first appeared in a trailer back in E3 2019, seen stabbing Radahn with their spears. Known as Noble Rot Knight in other languages, likely referring to the Botritis fungus that's used to make sweet wines Spear Variants are more aggressive than their Scythe wielding counterparts, often being the ones charging their opponents

sections.heading: Lore Items Related to Cleanrot Knight
sections.text: Cleanrot Helm Winged helm of the Cleanrot Knights, celebrated for their undefeated campaign in the Shattering. The Cleanrot Knights vowed to fight alongside Malenia, despite the inevitable, if gradual, putrefaction of their flesh. Their acceptance of their fate made these battles fiercest of all' . Cleanrot Knight's Sword Piercing sword of the Cleanrot Knights who fought alongside ' Malenia, Blade of Miquella. Mainly used as a backup weapon, in combination with a long-' handled armament' . Cleanrot Spear Spear of the Cleanrot Knights who fought alongside Malenia, Blade of Miquella. The winged golden blade deals holy damage. The diminutive shield is blessed with an incantation that wards off rot. Halo Scythe War scythe of the Cleanrot Knights who fought alongside Malenia, Blade of Miquella. This was the weapon of commanders in Malenia's army, and the half-halo blade deals holy damage' . Winged Sword Insignia A talisman depicting a raised prosthetic blade. An honor bestowed upon the knights who fought alongside Malenia the Severed. Raises attack power with successive attacks. The wings symbolize Malenia and her undefeated prowess. Though she never knew relief from the accursed rot she was born into, her blade was forever beautiful - and relentless' . Cleanrot Knight Finlay Ashes Legendary ashen remains. ' Use to summon the spirit of the Cleanrot Knight Finlay. Finlay was one of the few survivors of the Battle of Aeonia, who in an unimaginable act of heroism carried the slumbering demigod Malenia all the way back to the Haligtree. She managed the feat alone, fending off all manner of foes along the way.

sections.heading: Elden Ring Commander Gaius Boss Guide
sections.text: Commander Gaius Boss Video Guide Commander Gaius Fight Strategy The Best Tips for Commander Gaius: Use the Black Knife Tiche Ash Summons Opt for a Great Hammer like the Heavy Curved Great Club Bring Flask of Wondrous Physick ( Greenburst Crystal Tear and Opaline Hardtear or Windy Crystal Tear ) Item Use Crucible Feather Talisman to make dodging his charge easier Melee Users Before you begin the fight, make sure to replenish your Flask by resting at the nearest Site of Grace. You can also prepare your loadout by equipping the Flask of Wondrous Physick and using it with the Greenburst Crystal Tear and Opaline Hardtear to give you a temporary boost to all damage negation and stamina recovery speed. Once these items are ready, you can now head towards the fight. As soon as you walk into the arena, make sure to summon Black Knife Tiche . This is an Ash Summon with immunity to all Status Effects and is the ideal summon for this fight. Commander Gaius rides a giant wild boar that can rush forward in great speed. You will be battling both the rider and the Wild Boar here, and they can combine their attacks as you take them on. For melee users, the key to this fight is heavy attacks and jump attacks. This trades off defense for a chance to break the boss' stance and deal additional damage. While fighting this boss, try to stick to its sides and back. This gives you the best chances to avoid getting damaged especially during the first phase. The boss doesn't use a lot of its gravity attacks early on but will rely mostly on Standard damage type with its weapon swings. To begin, Commander Gaius will always open the fight with the Wild Boar Rush as you enter the arena, which is a move where he charges at you as you enter the arena. You can dodge by rolling into him at the very last second. While you are near this boss, it can use Wild Swing together with a Kick and Head Slam from the wild boar. If you're feeling confident, you can roll towards the swing of the weapon, and toward the Wild Boar for the Head Slam. The kick is a little difficult to dodge because it gives very little time to react. However, you can anticipate this attack if you spend too much time attacking from behind. Each time the boss finishes its string of attacks, prepare for a heavy or jump attack. This is your chance for retaliation and an opportunity to break its stance. The boss' second phase will begin once its health drops to about 50%. You will notice this when the boss clutches its body as the purple color mixed with lightning courses throughout his armor. During this phase, the boss will start using all of its gravity attacks and its basic attacks will deal additional gravity damage. These attacks are easily discernible because his weapon will glow purple, and you can hear a crackling audio cue as it charges up. There are about 5 Gravity attacks that we saw when we took down this boss, and one of the most dangerous ones is the Gravity Plunge . This is an attack that begins with a jump toward the sky, the boss will spin in place to charge the attack and plunge at high speed. The impact has a pretty wide AoE, so you shouldn't underestimate it. Ideally, you want to roll backward and away from the impact, but in situations where you prefer a high-risk/high-reward scenario, you can try to roll forward as the boss plunges and pull off a jump attack while the boss recovers from the impact. The other gravity attack worth mentioning is the Gravity Thrust , this is a move that he does where he charges up his weapon with gravity magic and then makes an upward thrust with it, creating an AoE damage within the area around him. When he does this, roll forward to dodge and you can retaliate with a light attack. Commander Gaius deals primarily physical damage and moderate amounts of magic damage. A greatshield with full physical block and high Guard Boost stats can block every attack Gaius can throw, making him extremely vulnerable to guard-counter loadouts; about 6 guard counters with a katana can cause the first stance break. Final Tips: Don't forget to consume your Flask of Wondrous Physick and summon Black Knife Tiche at the start. The bonus stamina recovery speed and damage negation will help in this fight. Summoning Black Knife Tiche is only recommended for players who don't require FP in Combat as it consumes 132 FP but will greatly benefit you against Commander Gaius. Alternatively, you may also use Cerulean Hidden Tear in your physick if you don't have the required FP for Black Knife Tiche (this eliminates all FP consumption). Magic and Ranged Users Use your buffs before entering the boss area. Wait a second before summoning spirit ashes after entering the boss area or the summoning may fail. You may summon Torrent, but the fight is generally easier without him. Gaius' boar is much faster than Torrent, and Gaius can kill Torrent very easily, leaving you vulnerable to a follow-up attack. It is also generally safer to stay in melee range. The fight wi

sections.heading: Lore Items Related to Commander Gaius
sections.text: Gaius's Greaves Black iron greaves made for Commander Gaius. A cruel joke, for he could not wear them. Riding atop the boar he called his other half, Gaius was in fact a warrior of albinauric extraction. Blades of Stone Gravity-manipulating sorcery of Commander Gaius. Pulls blade-like clumps of rock from the earth. Charge to form three successive clumps. Gaius and Radahn were good rivals in their youth, and this sorcery is a product of their friendly competition. Remembrance of the Wild Boar Rider Remembrance of Commander Gaius, hewn into the Scadutree. The power of its namesake can be unlocked by the Finger Reader. Alternatively, it can be used to gain a great bounty of runes. Both were as elder brothers to the lion, and both were cursed from birth. In spite of, or perhaps because of this very reason, Gaius was both Messmer's friend and the leader of his men. sections.heading: Elden Ring Commander Niall Boss Guide
sections.text: Commander Niall Fight Strategy The Best Tips for Commander Niall Niall will primarily focus on buffing his allies while they are still alive and will perform relatively simple attacks that are easily avoided. Focus on the dual greatsword Knight with at the beginning, as it is more aggressive than the shield Knight. Charming one of the Knights with Bewitching Branches can make the first phase quite simple. Use a tanky Spirit to distract the Banished Knights. Take advantage of when Niall tires himself out after his Charged Whirlwind dash move You can jump to avoid his shockwave foot stomp. Kill at least one Knight before summoning your spirit. Killing the last of his knights while he is in his buffing animation will lock him in his first phase until about half health Using kukris/throwing knives or ranged attacks triggers him to do his kick attack, if done correctly he can be put into a "positive feedback loop" in which he will jump attack you forever as long as you dodge into throwing a knife at him Backstabbing one Knight at the start of the fight, preferably buffed by the Dagger Talisman , is an effective way of dealing with the Knights quickly. A rare glitch may occur if the user is struck right before entering the arena, causing the boss to freeze. General Fight Strategy Commander Niall is accompanied by two Spectral Banished Knights , one equipped with dual greatswords and the other equipped with a sword and shield. Success in this battle hinges on your ability to manage the two very dangerous knights. Niall himself doesn't get too dangerous until the knights are defeated. He will lumber around the arena, making no real effort to close the distance so focus on the knights at the beginning. Of the two, the dual sword knight is the most aggressive and dangerous. It is highly recommended that you summon a tanky spirit to more easily manage both knights at once. They are also susceptible to Magic Damage so Sorcery mains should have a slight advantage damage-wise. The easiest way to be rid of the Banished Knights is to, immediately, after traversing the fog, run into the right-hand corner of the arena and await the charge of the dual-wielding Knight, and using a Bewitching Branch on him, turning him into an ally (it might take a few tries to get the timing right, the animation is rather long). This will cause the sword-n-board Banished Knight to immediately aggro him, while your new ally attacks Niall himself, ripping away a huge chunk of his health. Bewitch the second Banished Knight, while avoiding Niall's windstorm attacks, back away and summon your spirit ashes and apply any buff you need. Niall should have taken out both knights by this point (he kills them extremely quickly), or they will have brought him below 50% health, at which point they will despawn, as Niall enters his second phase. Once the knights are killed, Niall begins actively pursuing you and using his more dangerous moves. Niall commands the powers of Ice via a whirlwind he summons around him, as well as Lightning via infusions on his prosthetic leg. Niall's most dangerous moves always involve him summoning whirlwinds of frost around him. He can then follow up with a stomp of his peg leg, infusing it with lightning and then leaping towards you to perform a powerful leg smash that creates a lightning shockwave on impact. He can also follow-up with two versions of a dash attack. The first is a single whirl of his halberd followed by a quick dash into an uppercut with his halberd. The second version sees Niall charging up for a few seconds as he sucks in frosty winds towards him, he then whirls his halberd several times, creating an expanding whirlwind of frost. Finally, he dashes to the side and then runs toward you, culminating in an uppercut with his halberd. This move tires Niall out and he will be kneeling and vulnerable for several seconds. This is the biggest damage window throughout his fight so be sure to dodge the uppercut and get as many hits in as possible as he recovers. Melee Users Start with heavy R2 On right summon dual wielding knight, the attack should land at or just before he materializes. Then a second heavy R2, and he should stagger. If lucky, you can get a crit in which should kill him at appropriate level for this boss and you will be invulnerable. Roll away and or heal. Next bait out the 2nd summon and do a running R2, back up, rinse and repeat. If he teleports to you, roll behind him. Be selective. Running R2 should bait him into an attack and an auto stagger when he is walking with his shield up. You have plenty of time on the 2nd summon as the boss will be passive during this phase. Next the Commander Niall will charge up frost and electric attacks after his summons have died. Roll at the last second for his attacks. When he charges his leg and flip kicks, roll to his right (your left) to get an opening for an attack. He does a delayed heavy swing after one consecutive attack he has where you should roll twice i

sections.heading: Lore Items Related to Commander Niall
sections.text: Veteran's Prosthesis Bladed prosthetic leg enwreathed with the power of lightning, instead attached to the fist. Commander Niall, veteran of Castle Sol, offered this prosthesis in exchange for the lives of defeated knights held prisoner. He went on to lead these men as an army of no nation. Veteran's Armor Old armor that has seen many battles. Worn by Niall, the veteran general of Sol. Niall was a lone survivor who commanded spirits to defend his long-passed master. This aging general could not die, nor did he have anywhere to fade away.

sections.heading: Elden Ring Commander O'Neil Boss Guide
sections.text: Commander O'Neil Fight Strategy The Best Tips for Commander O'Neil: Use any tanky Spirit Ash Summons, as they will likely draw the most attention from the boss and his allies. Use the Rock Sling Spell, which can easily be obtained in the nearby ruins . Bring equipment inflicting Frostbite or/and Hemorrhage. Sneak up to O'Neil, which can be done with ease. This allows to perform few attacks before he even try to summon. Riding Torrent during this fight is recommended to avoid Scarlet Rot build up You can sneak up behind him and cast poison mist O'Neil cannot jump, so you can summon Latenna or use ranged bows on a tree branch to whittle him down. His crossbow summons in phase 1 will knock Latenna off the branch however, and his phase 2 summons can kill her. It is also possible for her to slowly inch forward and fall down within reach of O'Neil. Melee Users Direct Melee confrontation is possible, but it's much easier completing this fight on horseback. Employing a hit and run strategy will allow you to outrun Commander O'Neil's counter attacks as well as any attacks from his minions. This also has the added benefit of allowing you to travel outside the arena and avoid the scarlet rot build-up. Killing summoned Exile Crossbowmen and Exile Axe Soldiers is straightforward from horseback and can be performed without engaging with Commander O'Neil. Doing so will minimize the potential of being staggered or blindsided while attacking O'Neil and will simplify the fight. He will summon a second group of summons wielding axes during his second phase. Although they lack range, they will move towards you aggressively and will do more damage than the first group. However, they can also be dealt with relatively quickly on horseback. If you want to beat him on foot, it is also doable, since most of his attacks are easily parryable. You just have to watch out for the summons and the Rot Storm. You can kite him out to the nearby Site of Grace, then kite him through the Scarlet Rot geysers to damage him; he needs to be walking through the geyser when it erupts to take damage, the large pool of Scarlet Rot doesn't affect him. He will teleport back to the starting point for his second phase, and can be kited out to the geysers again. The second group of summons will likely follow him out, and that's a good time to use your Spirits to eliminate the summons. Magic and Ranged Users Magic users with long-ranged spells can easily outrange Commander O'Neil by fighting on horseback, trivializing the fight. He is a slow-moving boss that lumbers across the battlefield and makes no real effort to close the distance. Just make sure to clear his minions out whenever he summons them to avoid getting overwhelmed. Commander O'Neil Attacks & Counters Attack Description Counter Call Spirits - Exile Crossbowmen Commander O'Neil will summon 5 Exile Crossbowmen to provide fire support at the beginning of the battle. Each has roughly 430 health. First, kite Commander O'Neil away from the archers while dodging or blocking their shots. Take the minions out before refocusing on the commander. Call Spirits - Exile Greataxe Soldiers Commander O'Neil will summon 3 Exile Axe Soldiers when he drops to 40% health. Each soldier has roughly 500 health. The axe soldiers move faster than Commander O'Neil does. Keep away from Commander O'Neil as you deal with the axe men, while dodging out when he gets within striking distance. Glory, Brave Knights! - Offensive Commander O'Neil will swing his Commander's Standard around in the air and exhort his summons to fight on, boosting their attack speed. This buff takes the form of a little red mist around the enemies, indicating heightened offensive capacity. Commander O'Neil does not do this attack when he has no summons. Additionally, Commander O'Neil is vulnerable to attack when he enters this animation, so potentially this can prove to be a good opportunity for damage. Glory, Brave Knights! - Defensive Commander O'Neil will swing his Commander's Standard around in the air and exhorts his summons to fight defensively, boosting their resilience and giving them additional health. This buff manifests as a white glowing circle on enemies, and grants them additional resilience to damage as well as small amount of bonus health. Commander O'Neil does not do this attack when he has no summons. Additionally, Commander O'Neil is vulnerable to attack when he enters this animation, so potentially this can prove to be a good opportunity for damage. Rotting Whirlwind Commander O'Neil will kneel, and the wind around him will begin to blow harder as it forms a large area of effect around him. Then, he will swing his standard three times, doing massive damage to anything still inside his area of effect and building up huge amounts of Scarlet Rot, practically guaranteeing a proc. This attack takes about 4 seconds to come out, and if you're on horseback it's very easy to escape. Spearing Attack Commander O'Neil has a range of long-range

sections.heading: Elden Ring Count Ymir, Mother of Fingers Boss Guide
sections.text: Count Ymir, Mother of Fingers Boss Video Guide [video coming soon] Shadow of the Erdtree Bosses Ranked Count Ymir, Mother of Fingers Fight Strategy The Best Tips for Count Ymir, Mother of Fingers: Use spells that do Lightning damage, such as Lightning Spear Equip fast-hitting weapon types, such as Hand-to-Hand Arts and Fists Use weapons or spells that deal Fire Damage to quickly deal with the summoned Fingercreepers . Melee Users Count Ymir, Mother of Fingers can be encountered in the Cathedral of Manus Metyr . After defeating Metyr, Mother of Fingers , return to the Cathedral of Manus Metyr and interact with the throne again. Jolán will first invade, then Count Ymir will appear after she is defeated. This boss deals Magic Damage and can summons allies. Count Ymir has several sorceries up his sleeve, including Cherishing Fingers , this is where he lifts his staff and slams it back down to cast a ring of six fingers that surround him, this attack can be indicated when Count Ymir raises and slams his staff down directly. When the fingers come up, it will deal damage to you so you will need to dodge backward and attack his once the fingers go away. Another one is Glintstone Nails , in which Count Ymir will lift up his staff once again but wave it around to launch six tracking projectiles towards you. You can easily avoid this attack by simply sidestepping or perfectly timing your forward dodge roll to avoid the projectiles. You can also use the pillars around the area if you are having difficulties with dodging this attack. His last attack is Finger Spawn. Just like Metyr , he can also summon Fingercreepers , though the move is slow and it leaves him open to attack. Ymir will stay stationary while summoning. He will start groaning, and dark green liquid can be seen as Fingercreepers move out of his body. Just like for the Metyr boss fight, you can take those out first, so you won't be overwhelmed. Once Count Ymiris defeated, he will drop Ymir's Bell Bearing , the Maternal Staff , and the High Priest Set . Magic and Ranged Users Before the initial fight with Jolán, you can roll around the area and break all the benches. They can block projectiles and make it hard to quickly get away from Ymir. For Faith builds, Frenzied Burst can reach all the way across the arena. You can just stand at the opposite end of the cathedral from Ymir and blast away, he will usually just stay over there. The Fire Damage will also kill the Fingercreepers quickly. If you're feeling risky, Inescapable Frenzy can be used, though he is rather resistant to Madness . For Intelligence builds, Stars of Ruin or Star Shower can keep him on the defensive. Use attacks like Carian Greatsword or Adula's Moonblade to deal with the adds. Carian Piercer can easily roll-catch Ymir and knock him down. For ranged users, consider using Fire Arrows or Explosive Bolts to deal with the Fingercreepers. Otherwise, be wary of his Cherishing Fingers deflecting any of your projectiles. Rancor Shot with the Bone Bow or Enchanted Shot can land some hits from afar. Count Ymir, Mother of Fingers Attacks & Counters Attack Description Counter Staff Strike While in melee range, Ymir may use their staff to club the player, dealing minuscule damage. A weak attack that is rarely used, but can interrupt your own attacks. Keep wailing on him to prevent him from counter-attacking. Finger Spawn Much like Metyr, Ymir reaches into his chest and births a Lesser Fingercreeper to assist him in combat. Ymir gains a lot of poise when performing this move and is unable to be backstabbed, but it leaves him open to attacks. Get some hits in and then deal with the spawned Fingercreeper, preferably using Fire. Cherishing Fingers Ymir slams his staff into the ground, causing six fingers to erupt from the ground and encircle him, dealing damage. He may charge this spell, increasing its damage and size. While active, most projectiles, whether physical or magical, will be warded. Ymir often casts this spell when in melee range. Roll backward once you get a couple of hits in. Glintstone Nails Lifts up his staff to launch six white projectiles that slowly move but heavily track the player. Avoid taking the brunt of this attack head on. Roll forward to make most of the projectiles hit the ground and disappear instead of looping around. Miriam's Vanishing Ymir waves his staff, suddenly vanishing into blue mist and reappearing further away. Often used to escape melee range. This spell often messes with your lock-on. He only teleports a short distance away, so keep watch. Dear Yuri, dear Fingers!" After Fight: "Forgive me,
